context: The figure matches the code: on a 4×4 board (n = 4), row increases from top to bottom and col from left to right, both starting at 0. The queen is at zero-based coordinates (1, 1), the second row and second column. In the Boolean arrays, T means occupied and F means free.
description: Squares on the same main diagonal share row − col, and squares on the same secondary diagonal share row + col. For a candidate (row, col), index the three arrays by col, row − col + n − 1, and row + col, respectively. Place a queen only if all three entries are F. With n = 4, row − col ranges from −3 to 3. Adding 3 gives nonnegative indices from 0 to 6.
Set the three entries to T on placement and restore them to F when backtracking. The two tables give the indexing rules and the full contents of all three arrays.

frames.explanation: The Boolean arrays cols, diags1, and diags2 let us check the column and both diagonals for conflicts in constant time. In general, an n×n board has n columns and 2n − 1 diagonals in each direction.
frames.title: Tracking queen constraints with three Boolean arrays

summary: Use zero-based row and column coordinates to track and check occupied lines in the column array cols and the diagonal arrays diags1 and diags2.
